LEARNING PATH ROADMAP · Web Application Security

Your roadmap in Web Application Security.

Explore the courses in this learning path and the order of modules within each one.

1 course 12 lessons ~26 min reading Client-Side Progress
RECOMMENDED STARTING COURSE

Web Security Foundations

Beginners, students, and developers who want to understand web security before studying individual vulnerabilities.

Start this course View path overview

Before you start

  • Comfort using a web browser and navigating websites.
  • No previous security-testing experience required. Basic HTML is helpful, not required.
CORE COMPETENCIES

What you will master in this path

Targeted capabilities and verifiable mental models you will build across each module.

Architecture

Attack Surface & HTTP Flow

Chart system assets, HTTP messages, cookies, and server-side defensive trust boundaries.

Identity

Authentication, Sessions & Access

Safeguard logins, manage session lifecycles, and eliminate IDOR and privilege escalation.

Injection & XSS

Parameterized Queries & Encoding

Neutralize SQL injection, reflected/stored/DOM XSS, and enforce strict Content Security Policy.

Hardening

CSRF, SSRF & Production Controls

Enforce SameSite/CSRF tokens, egress allowlists, safe file uploads, security headers, and rate limits.

CURRICULUM TIMELINE

Courses and their module order

Follow modules in order. Each milestone cements foundational concepts before advancing.

COURSE MILESTONES

Web Security Foundations

12 lessons · 26 min

A complete 4-module foundation: start with HTTP and trust boundaries, protect sessions and authorization, eliminate SQL injection and XSS, and harden CSRF, SSRF, uploads, and production APIs.

  1. 1

    Understand the web

    Module 1
    Milestone outcome:

    You can trace a request and identify the boundary where a security decision belongs.

    Build the mental model first: what needs protecting and how requests move through an application.

    1Web Application Security Fundamentals3m→2HTTP Requests & Responses3m→
  2. 2

    Protect identity & access

    Module 2
    Milestone outcome:

    You can distinguish a login problem from an authorization problem and explain the relevant defenses.

    Build on HTTP to understand who a user is, how a session persists, and what that user may do.

    1Authentication & Session Security2m→2Access Control & Authorization2m→
  3. 3

    Injection, XSS & Client-Side Defenses

    Module 3
    Milestone outcome:

    You can separate untrusted data from executable queries, HTML templates, and browser DOM sinks.

    Why mixing untrusted input with code interpreters causes SQL injection, cross-site scripting, and DOM vulnerabilities — and how parameterization, context-aware encoding, and CSP stop them.

    1SQL Injection & Parameterized Queries2m→2Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Contexts & CSP2m→3DOM-Based Vulnerabilities & Sanitization2m→
  4. 4

    CSRF, SSRF & Production Hardening

    Module 4
    Milestone outcome:

    You can design defense-in-depth controls for state-changing requests, outbound network calls, file storage, and production APIs.

    Protect cross-origin state changes, outbound server fetches, file uploads, HTTP response headers, and API endpoints in production.

    1CSRF, SameSite Cookies & State-Changing Requests2m→2SSRF & Outbound Request Controls2m→3File Upload Validation & Storage Isolation2m→4Security Headers, CORS & TLS Deployment2m→5API Rate Limiting, Logging & Defensive Verification2m→
